Quick Summary

William H. McNeill's The Rise of the West (1963) offers a broad perspective on the history of human civilization, tracing the development and interactions of various cultures over 5,000 years. McNeill argued that all cultures influence and are influenced by others, emphasizing constant change and cultural diffusion throughout history. He posited that European civilization's global preeminence since 1500 CE stemmed from its inherent instability and dynamic quality, which allowed it to overcome the established balance of Eastern civilizations.
